👩‍🦳 Menopause-related changes to the body may happen suddenly, rather than being a gradual part of aging, a new study shows.  Researchers analysed the results of over 300 million lab tests - for bone health, liver and kidney function, the immune system, and more. Around the time of menopause, the results of more than half of the tests tended to suddenly shift for women, whereas changes happened gradually in men. However, the size of the sudden changes was smaller in women taking menopausal hormonal therapy. The researchers also found that levels of reproductive hormones started changing over a decade before women's periods stopped.

🗨️ University of the Sunshine Coast, The University of Melbourne, and Macquarie University experts have responded to the research.
